message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# Replace <PROJECT_ID> and <ZONE> with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server   # optional networking tags
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GiB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` requests one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` + `--image-project` | Installs the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root SSD. 100 GB is a good starting point. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud‑Platform scope so the VM can use other GCP services if needed. |
| `--tags` | Optional network tags for firewall rules. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine family, change `--machine-type` and `--accelerator`.  
> **Tip:** To see available zones that support A6000, run `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(zone)"`.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint (e.g., from a custom script), here’s the minimal JSON body you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y build-essential" }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your actual project ID and zone.  
Make sure you have an OAuth token (`<YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>`) with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

---

## Quick Checklist

- ✅ Verify that the chosen zone supports `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.
- ✅ Ensure you have enough quota for GPUs in that zone.
- ✅ Check that your billing account is active.
- ✅ Optionally add firewall rules to allow SSH (port 22) and any other ports you need.

Once the instance is created, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=${PROJECT_ID} --zone=${ZONE}
```

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
